title: Outdated phone? Just opening a website was enough to get robbed
description:
Outdated iPhone or Android? Opening one website was enough to get robbed.

Security firm Sekoia reported on November 4, 2026 a campaign it calls "Poisoned Source". Sekoia links it, with "moderate to high confidence", to APT29, an intrusion set widely attributed to Russia's foreign intelligence service. Attack code was planted on real websites and on fake lookalike sites, and a web analytics script, the Plerdy SEO tracker, was hijacked between August 27 and September 3, 2026.

The code profiled each visitor's phone first. Outdated iPhones (iOS 16.7 and iOS 18.5) and Android phones running Chrome 139 to 145 were served exploit chains that stole browser cookies and, on some devices, messages, photos, Wi-Fi passwords and more. No click was needed.

One of the bugs, CVE-2024-27834, was fixed by Apple in May 2024. On November 4, 2026, the US agency CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Analyst note: there are no zero-days here. Sekoia says all three exploit chains rely on known, already-patched vulnerabilities, and that a user running an up-to-date operating system is safe from these attacks.

Do this tonight:
1. iPhone: Settings, then General, then Software Update.
2. Android: update Chrome in the Google Play Store, and install any system update.
3. Turn on automatic updates.
